answers.how: Measured the astronaut's vertical height in pixels (~336 px = 2.2 m, giving 0.00655 m/px) and tracked the astronaut's centroid displacement across frames 10 to 14 around t=0.5s (vx ≈ 1.85 m/s, vy ≈ 0.46 m/s).
Computed the rate of change of velocity around t=0.5s (frames 5 to 16) as the astronaut decelerates vertically before landing, using the scale derived from the astronaut's 2.2 m height.
Tracked the astronaut's centroid between frames 22 and 26 around t=1.0s during the upward jump (vx ≈ 5.07 m/s, vy ≈ -1.83 m/s) and converted from pixels using the 2.2 m height prior.
Calculated the magnitude of velocity change per unit time around t=1.0s (frames 21 to 32) as the astronaut transitions from the push-off peak into the ballistic arc.
Measured the astronaut's displacement across frames 46 to 50 around t=2.0s (vx ≈ 2.04 m/s, vy ≈ 0.90 m/s) and scaled by 0.00655 m/px.
Estimated the downward gravitational acceleration and horizontal velocity change around t=2.0s (frames 42 to 53) during the descending phase of the jump.
Tracked the astronaut's centroid across frames 70 to 74 around t=3.0s (vx ≈ 1.36 m/s, vy ≈ -0.20 m/s) using the scale from the 2.2 m height prior.
Measured the rate of change of the astronaut's velocity vector across frames 68 to 79 around t=3.0s using the 0.00655 m/px scale factor.
